title: Tale of the Fisherman and His Son (ಕನ್ನಡ)

keywords: tale of the fisherman and his son
full_text:
On the rocky coast of the Persian Gulf lived an elderly fisherman named Jabir and his bright young son, Tariq. For forty years Jabir had cast his solitary net into the sea, catching only enough sardines and mullet to stave off starvation.

One evening, seeing his father's weary shoulders and trembling fingers, Tariq said:
'Father, the sea is vast, yet thou fishest only in the shallow breakers where other boats have already disturbed the schools. Let us study the flight of the sea-gulls and the currents of the deep shoals.'

Tariq observed that every afternoon, flocks of white gulls gathered around a submerged coral reef two miles offshore, diving into the blue water.
The boy constructed a small, light outrigger from driftwood, fitted it with a woven reed sail, and persuaded his father to sail to the reef before dawn.

Casting their nets above the deep reef waters, they hauled up nets teeming with magnificent red snapper and kingfish, which fetched ten times the price of shore sardines in the harbor market!

With their first earnings, Tariq did not buy luxuries. He bought strong hemp ropes and cedar planks to build a seaworthy fishing smack, and invited five elderly, impoverished fishermen of their village to join their crew as equal partners.

Within two years, their small cooperative fleet provided fresh fish to the entire provincial capital. When a severe winter storm threatened to destroy the harbor boats, Tariq's knowledge of the coastal reefs enabled him to guide all twenty village vessels safely into a sheltered tidal lagoon.

The Governor of the province appointed Tariq Chief Warden of the Fisheries. Jabir sat upon the harbor terrace in warm wool robes, watching his son manage the port with wisdom and benevolence, thanking heaven for a son whose clever mind and loving heart brought prosperity to an entire coast.
moral: Wisdom shared across generations transforms modest toil into enduring security and honor. [KN]
